title: Unbounded strict-system compact support and its projection comparison
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For $W=X,Y,\overline X$ and $\tau=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $\mathscr S_W^\tau$ be the category of strict systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves with semilinear quotient transitions and componentwise morphisms [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]; use its ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], exact evaluations $e_n$ and, for $m\ge n\ge1$, derived quotient functors $T^W_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Write $t^M_{m,n}:T^W_{m,n}M_m\to M_n$ for the scalar-extension adjunct of the actual transition. 
On the etale systems put $F=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$ and $F_n=Rp_{*,n}j_{!,n}$. This is an exact coproduct-preserving functor, with coproducts of systems as in [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension], with the canonical evaluation comparisons $e_nF\cong F_ne_n$ of the system direct-image and open-extension operations of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a_W:W\to s$. For every $P\in D(\mathscr S_s^{\mathrm{et}})$ and $M\in D(\mathscr S_X^{\mathrm{et}})$, the geometric counit and the open-extension tensor comparison define an actual natural system projection map [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]
$$\pi_{P,M}:a_Y^*P\otimes^L FM\longrightarrow F(a_X^*P\otimes^L M).$$
It is invertible and evaluates to the ordinary unbounded finite-coefficient projection map. The same construction for quotient coefficients defines canonical maps $q_{m,n}:T^Y_{m,n}F_m\to F_nT^X_{m,n}$, namely the coefficient projection comparison $b_{m,n}$ of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] for $Rp_{*,\bullet}$ composed with the termwise identification for $j_{!,\bullet}$. They are invertible on all unbounded inputs; they are maps in the changed-coefficient derived category, satisfy the quotient cocycle and give
$$t^{FM}_{m,n}=F_n(t^M_{m,n})q_{m,n,M_m}.$$
All maps are defined by the ringed sequence-site operations before evaluation. Their evaluation comparisons preserve the geometric inverse/direct-image units and counits. No boundedness assumption is made on $P$ or $M$.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] for the geometric morphism $p$ and the open localization $j$. They define $F=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$ on the ordinary unbounded category, and their evaluation comparisons compose to $e_nF\cong Rp_{*,n}j_{!,n}e_n=F_ne_n$. These comparisons preserve evaluated geometric units and counits. The system categories are Grothendieck and their derived direct images use K-injective resolutions, as in the cited theorem. Thus [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] makes $Rp_{*,\bullet}$ exact. Exact open extension induces an exact derived functor by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], so $F$ is exact. The functor and its comparisons are constructed on systems, rather than inferred from a diagram in the levelwise derived categories.

proof.text: The datum [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] makes every $A_n$ finite. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $Y$ Noetherian. The proper part $p$ is of finite type, so the same lemma makes $\overline X$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-etale-proper-derived-lower-star-coproducts-for-grothendieck] to $p$ and each $A_n$. Exact open extension preserves coproducts: its system adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] apply. For an arbitrary small family $(M_i)$, evaluate the canonical map $\bigoplus_i FM_i\to F(\bigoplus_i M_i)$. Componentwise coproducts and the comparisons of step 1 identify it with the canonical coproduct map for $Rp_{*,n}j_{!,n}$, hence with an isomorphism. Joint conservativity of the evaluations proves it is an isomorphism of derived systems, including for the empty family.

proof.text: On the ringed sequence topoi put $H=a_Y^*P$ and $N=j_{!,\bullet}M$. Form $H\otimes^LRp_{*,\bullet}N\to Rp_{*,\bullet}(p^*H\otimes^LN)$ by the counit transpose of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], with canonical tensor symmetries. To obtain the open tensor map, choose a flat-term K-flat representative $L$ of $p^*H$. Its open restriction is K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For any representative $C$ of $M$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] to every summand $j_!C^r\otimes L^s$. Their sum is the required chain isomorphism $j_!C\otimes L\cong j_!(C\otimes j^*L)$: $j_!$ preserves direct sums by its adjunction and step 2, and the sheaf isomorphism is natural in both factors, hence commutes with the signed differentials. Exactness of $j_!$ and the K-flat computations identify its localization with the open derived tensor comparison, independent of representatives. Follow the proper projection by $Rp_{*,\bullet}$ of this map. Pullback composition identifies $j^*p^*H=a_X^*P$. This defines the actual natural system map $\pi_{P,M}$. The evaluation normalization of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] identifies its evaluations with the ordinary counit-defined proper/open projection maps.

proof.text: For each $n$, apply [lem-etale-proper-projection-formula-finite] to $p$, $j_{!,n}M_n$ and $a_Y^*P_n$. Its finite-ring hypothesis was checked in step 2; its statement permits both inputs to be unbounded. Apply [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor] to $j$, $M_n$ and $p^*a_Y^*P_n$; this theorem also permits arbitrary unbounded inputs. Under the evaluation normalization of step 3, their composite is precisely $e_n\pi_{P,M}$. Both factors are invertible. Joint conservativity [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension] now makes $\pi_{P,M}$ invertible. This uses evaluation to detect an isomorphism of an already constructed map; it does not use evaluation to assert equality or existence of morphisms.

proof.text: For $m\ge n$ use the scalar mate $b_{m,n}$ constructed by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] for $p$. Apply [lem-asd-proper-finite-coefficient-extension] to $A_m\to A_n$, the proper $p$, and the arbitrary unbounded input $j_{!,m}M_m$. Its Noetherian and finite-ring hypotheses were checked in step 2. Its displayed counit transpose is exactly this $b_{m,n}$, and it proves invertibility in the changed-coefficient category itself, without assuming flatness of $A_n$ over $A_m$. Compose with $Rp_{*,n}$ of the canonical open scalar comparison from [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor]. This gives the stated $q_{m,n}:T^Y_{m,n}F_m\to F_nT^X_{m,n}$ as an actual changed-coefficient natural isomorphism. The open comparison is normalized by balancing on the open and zero off it; thus it is the termwise comparison stipulated in the item.

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings); the counit normalization is sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0B56, and the open factor is Tag 0GL1.

proof.text: For $l\ge m\ge n$, identify $T_{m,n}T_{l,m}\cong T_{l,n}$ by the canonical derived scalar associator. The pullback/scalar squares for $p$ paste to the square for $A_l\to A_n$: these are the composition comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] for the geometric and coefficient ringed-topos morphisms. Their coherence is induced by tensor reassociation and multiplication, sending $c\otimes(b\otimes x)$ to $cb\otimes x$. Mate pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], clause (1), therefore gives $b_{l,n}=b_{m,n}T_{l,m}\circ T_{m,n}b_{l,m}$ under the source and target associators. The open scalar comparisons satisfy the same successive-extension law by [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor]. Substitute these two identities in the proper/open definition of $q$ and use naturality of $b_{m,n}$ with respect to the open comparison. This yields $q_{l,n}=q_{m,n,T^X_{l,m}(-)}\circ T^Y_{m,n}(q_{l,m})$. For equal indices the pullback square and its mate are identities by clause (4) of the mate-pasting lemma, and the open comparison is the scalar unit. Thus the quotient cocycle and identity laws hold for the specified maps, in their actual Hom sets.

proof.text: The extension-form transition of $Rp_{*,\bullet}N$ is $Rp_{*,n}(t^N_{m,n})b_{m,n,N_m}$ by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Take $N=j_{!,\bullet}M$. Its transition is $j_{!,n}(t^M_{m,n})$ after the open scalar comparison, since this comparison is the termwise extension-by-zero balancing map [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor]. Substitution gives $t^{FM}_{m,n}=F_n(t^M_{m,n})q_{m,n,M_m}$, as asserted. The unit and counit compatibility is the one already supplied by the system evaluation comparisons in step 1. No step has imposed boundedness, normalization, finite Tor amplitude, or flatness of a coefficient quotient.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q116-977920fcd (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all seven steps and every cited statement. The delivery adds no new nodes, and the item statement and stmt_deps are identical to the live copy, where the item is still unsplit. There is no cycle; its only citer is lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates. No SGA source is used. Steps 1-2: exactness comes from lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated plus the termwise exact j_! (exact-functor-derived-factorization). Coproduct preservation comes from lem-etale-proper-derived-lower-star-coproducts-for-grothendieck, with A_n finite by def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension(4) and Y and X̄ Noetherian by finite-type-over-noetherian. Coproducts are componentwise and evaluations are jointly conservative (lem-pur-system-level-left-extension). Steps 3-4: π is built on the sequence topoi from the counit transpose of ringed-projection-mate-exact and the 0GL1 chain computation via ringed-slice-extension-tensor. Its evaluations are the level maps (semilinear-derived-sections), which are invertible by 0F0G (lem-etale-proper-projection-formula-finite, unbounded) and lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor. Step 5: b_{m,n} is literally the β_L of lem-asd-proper-finite-coefficient-extension, invertible without flatness; the open factor is q_j from lem-coef-etale-open-tensor. Step 6: the cocycle follows from mate-pasting clauses (1) and (4) plus canonical pullback-composition coherence, written out. Step 7: the extension-form transition formula plus the j_! balancing gives t^{FM}=F_n(t^M)q. Small cases checked: identity f, zero input or empty coproduct, nonflat Z/l^2→Z/l, unbounded inputs. Batch-5: both flagged citations are general finite-ring étale facts (Stacks 0F0G and 0F11-type coproducts), not steps of the trace formula or Poincaré duality. Their closures meet those chapters only in generic nodes (lisse=module objects, schematically dense open, limit descent and others), so I accept them, as in earlier reviews (Q129/Q29/Q18). Advisories: (1) the slice lemma is applied to the constant sequence h_U, which is not representable; the identity holds by topos localization or level by level, so this is elementary. (2) Steps 5-6 overlap the existing unsplit lem-pur-etale-system-coefficient-projection (q_a with cocycle on étale systems), which could have been cited; this is not a fault. The 13 split_report tool_uses are generic and accepted.
